title: CHAPTER 12: PRACTICE MCQs FOR HP COMPETITIVE EXAMS

blocks.content: These multiple-choice questions are specifically designed for HP Police SI, HP PSC, HP Patwari, HP Clerk, HP TET, and all other HP state competitive examinations. Each answer includes the key fact for quick learning.

items: On which date was Himachal Pradesh granted full statehood?     (a) 15 April 1948  (b) 1 November 1956  (c) 25 January 1971  (d) 1 September 1972     Answer: (c) 25 January 1971 – HP became the 18th state of India on Republic Day.

Who was the first Chief Minister of Himachal Pradesh?     (a) Thakur Ram Lal  (b) Shanta Kumar  (c) Virbhadra Singh  (d) Dr. Y.S. Parmar     Answer: (d) Dr. Y.S. Parmar – served as CM from 1952 and worked for HP's statehood.
The Kangra Fort was captured by which Mughal Emperor's forces?     (a) Akbar  (b) Jahangir  (c) Shah Jahan  (d) Aurangzeb     Answer: (b) Jahangir – in 1620 CE, captured by general Shaikh Farid.

The Kullu Dussehra was initiated by which ruler and in which year?     (a) Raja Jagat Singh, 1660 CE  (b) Raja Sansar Chand, 1780 CE  (c) Raja Man Singh, 1720 CE  (d) Raja Prithvi Chand, 1640 CE     Answer: (a) Raja Jagat Singh, 1660 CE – started the tradition of bringing Raghunath deity.

Which treaty transferred the HP hill territories from Sikh rule to British?     (a) Treaty of Amritsar (1809)  (b) Treaty of Lahore (1846)  (c) Treaty of Bhyrowal (1846)  (d) Treaty of Simla (1914)     Answer: (b) Treaty of Lahore, 1846 – after the First Anglo-Sikh War.

Sansar Chand of Kangra was defeated by the Gurkhas at which battle?     (a) Aut  (b) Nadaun  (c) Mahal Morian  (d) Sujanpur     Answer: (c) Mahal Morian, 1806 CE – ended Sansar Chand's expansionary phase.

The Chamba kingdom was founded around 920 CE. Who founded it and what is its naming story?     (a) Raja Sahil Varman; named after daughter Champavati  (b) Raja Meru Varman; named after Champa flower  (c) Raja Prithvi Varman; named after a sage  (d) Raja Ajay Varman; named after Chandrabhaga River     Answer: (a) Raja Sahil Varman; named after his daughter Champavati.

Who is called the 'Apple Man of Himachal Pradesh'?     (a) A.J. Oakley  (b) Captain Kennedy  (c) Dr. Samuel Stokes (Satyanand Stokes)  (d) Sansar Chand     Answer: (c) Dr. Samuel Stokes (Satyanand Stokes) – planted Delicious apple varieties at Thanedar, Shimla.

When was HP initially formed as a Chief Commissioner's Province?     (a) 15 August 1947  (b) 15 April 1948  (c) 26 January 1950  (d) 1 November 1956     Answer: (b) 15 April 1948 – formed by merging 31 princely states and 4 chieftainships.

The Shanan Power Project (1926) at Jogindernagar was the first hydropower project in HP. It is on which river?     (a) Beas  (b) Sutlej  (c) Uhl (a tributary of Beas)  (d) Ravi     Answer: (c) Uhl River – a tributary of Beas; still operating.

Which hill kingdom is considered one of the oldest royal dynasties in the world?     (a) Mandi (Sen dynasty)  (b) Kullu (Raghuvanshi)  (c) Kangra (Katoch dynasty)  (d) Chamba (Varman dynasty)     Answer: (c) Kangra – Katoch dynasty claims 3,500+ years of lineage.

Mandi Conspiracy Case (1914) is associated with which freedom fighter?     (a) Shiv Nand Ramaul  (b) Bhai Hirda Ram  (c) Padam Dev  (d) Thakur Sen Negi     Answer: (b) Bhai Hirda Ram – plotted against British rule in Mandi; considered HP's earliest revolutionary.
The first Governor-General to visit Simla was:     (a) Lord Dalhousie  (b) Lord Dufferin  (c) Lord Amherst  (d) Lord Curzon     Answer: (c) Lord Amherst – visited Simla in 1827.
Simla was made the official summer capital of British India by:     (a) Lord Dalhousie  (b) Lord Dufferin  (c) Lord Canning  (d) Lord Ripon     Answer: (b) Lord Dufferin – in 1864.

The Shimla Agreement of 1972 (post-1971 war between India and Pakistan) was signed at which building?     (a) HP Vidhan Sabha  (b) Viceregal Lodge (now Rashtrapati Niwas/IIAS)  (c) Peterhoff  (d) Gorton Castle     Answer: (b) Viceregal Lodge (now known as Rashtrapati Niwas) – signed by Indira Gandhi and Zulfikar Ali Bhutto.
The highest peak of Himachal Pradesh is:     (a) Deo Tibba  (b) Reo Purgyil  (c) Shigri Parbat  (d) Hanuman Tibba     Answer: (b) Reo Purgyil – 6816 m; in Kinnaur district on the HP-Tibet border.

Which dam on the Sutlej River created the Gobind Sagar Lake?     (a) Pandoh Dam  (b) Pong Dam  (c) Bhakra Dam  (d) Nathpa Jhakri Dam     Answer: (c) Bhakra Dam – in Bilaspur; one of the tallest gravity dams in India.

The Atal Tunnel connects:     (a) Shimla to Kinnaur  (b) Manali (Kullu) to Lahaul  (c) Chamba to Pangi  (d) Mandi to Spiti     Answer: (b) Manali (Kullu) to Lahaul – 8.9 km; world's longest highway tunnel above 10,000 ft.

Sutlej River enters Himachal Pradesh from Tibet through which pass?     (a) Rohtang Pass  (b) Kunzum La  (c) Jalori Pass  (d) Shipkila Pass     Answer: (d) Shipkila Pass – in Kinnaur; important trade point with China.
The largest district of HP by area is:     (a) Kangra  (b) Chamba  (c) Shimla  (d) Lahaul-Spiti     Answer: (d) Lahaul-Spiti – 13,835 sq km; about 25% of HP's total area.
Which lake in HP is called 'Moon Lake' due to its crescent shape?     (a) Renuka Lake  (b) Chandratal  (c) Surajtal  (d) Prashar Lake     Answer: (b) Chandratal – in Lahaul-Spiti at 4,250 m altitude.

Maharana Pratap Sagar (Pong Dam Lake) on the Beas River is a:     (a) National Park  (b) Ramsar Wetland Site  (c) Biosphere Reserve  (d) UNESCO Heritage Site     Answer: (b) Ramsar Wetland Site – important for migratory birds; in Kangra district.
Which is the largest natural lake in HP?     (a) Chandratal  (b) Prashar Lake  (c) Renuka Lake  (d) Rewalsar Lake     Answer: (c) Renuka Lake – in Sirmaur district; associated with Goddess Renuka.

Bara Shigri Glacier is located in which district of HP?     (a) Kinnaur  (b) Chamba  (c) Lahaul-Spiti  (d) Kullu     Answer: (c) Lahaul-Spiti – Lahaul sub-division; second longest glacier in India (~25 km).

The Rohtang Pass (3978 m) connects:     (a) Spiti to Lahaul  (b) Kullu Valley (Manali) to Lahaul  (c) Chamba to Pangi  (d) Kinnaur to Spiti     Answer: (b) Kullu Valley (Manali) to Lahaul – key tourist and strategic pass.
Which river originates from Beas Kund near Rohtang Pass?     (a) Sutlej  (b) Ravi  (c) Chenab  (d) Beas     Answer: (d) Beas – originates at Beas Kund at approximately 4000 m altitude.

Dharamshala receives approximately how much annual rainfall?     (a) 800 mm  (b) 1200 mm  (c) 3400 mm  (d) 500 mm     Answer: (c) ~3400 mm – one of the wettest places in North India due to Dhauladhar Range.
Spiti Valley is a 'cold desert' receiving approximately how much annual rainfall?     (a) 500 mm  (b) 1000 mm  (c) 170 mm  (d) 2000 mm     Answer: (c) ~170 mm – rain shadow zone; arid conditions.
Which pass connects Lahaul to Spiti Valley?     (a) Rohtang Pass  (b) Baralacha La  (c) Kunzum La  (d) Jalori Pass     Answer: (c) Kunzum La – at 4590 m; Lahaul (Gramphu) to Spiti (Losar area).

Khajjiar is called 'Mini Switzerland of India'. It is located in which district?     (a) Kullu  (b) Chamba  (c) Mandi  (d) Shimla     Answer: (b) Chamba – at altitude 1920 m; deodar forest surrounding a meadow and lake.

blocks.content: Section C – HP Culture, Wildlife and Miscellaneous (25 Questions)

items: The State Tree of Himachal Pradesh is:     (a) Oak  (b) Rhododendron  (c) Deodar  (d) Blue Pine     Answer: (c) Deodar (Cedrus deodara) – sacred and economically important conifer.

The State Animal of Himachal Pradesh is:     (a) Himalayan Tahr  (b) Snow Leopard  (c) Musk Deer  (d) Bharal (Blue Sheep)     Answer: (b) Snow Leopard (Panthera uncia) – endangered; found in Lahaul-Spiti, Kinnaur.

The State Bird of HP (Western Tragopan) is locally known as:     (a) Monal  (b) Cheer Pheasant  (c) Koklass  (d) Jujurana     Answer: (d) Jujurana – also called 'King of birds'; endangered pheasant species.

Chamba Rumal is famous for what type of craft?     (a) Block printing  (b) Both-side identical hand embroidery  (c) Weaving  (d) Leather work     Answer: (b) Both-side identical hand embroidery – GI tagged; scenes from epics and Pahari painting themes.
The world's highest post office is at:     (a) Kaza, Spiti  (b) Hikkim, Spiti  (c) Tashigang, Spiti  (d) Nako, Kinnaur     Answer: (b) Hikkim, Spiti – at 14,567 feet (4,440 m).
The Tabo Monastery in Spiti was founded in:     (a) 800 CE  (b) 996 CE  (c) 1200 CE  (d) 1500 CE     Answer: (b) 996 CE – by Rinchen Zangpo; also called 'Ajanta of Himalayas'; over 1,000 years old.

Great Himalayan National Park in Kullu was declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in:     (a) 2000  (b) 2008  (c) 2014  (d) 2018     Answer: (c) 2014 – for its rich biodiversity including Western Tragopan and Snow Leopard.

The Kalka-Shimla Railway was included in UNESCO World Heritage Site (Mountain Railways of India) in:     (a) 2000  (b) 2004  (c) 2008  (d) 2012     Answer: (c) 2008 – along with Darjeeling Himalayan Railway and Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

The Mandi Shivratri Fair is popularly known as:     (a) State Shivratri Fair  (b) National Shivratri Fair  (c) International Shivratri Fair  (d) Himalayan Shivratri Fair     Answer: (c) International Shivratri Fair – hundreds of deities (devtas) gather from across the region.

World's highest cricket ground (2250 m) is located at:     (a) Manali  (b) Dharamshala  (c) Narkanda  (d) Chail (Solan)     Answer: (d) Chail, Solan – built in 1893 by Maharaja Bhupinder Singh of Patiala.

The Kangra Painting School is known for which predominant theme?     (a) Rajput warfare  (b) Krishna-Radha and nature  (c) Mughal court scenes  (d) Buddhist iconography     Answer: (b) Krishna-Radha and nature – lyrical naturalism; soft colors; patronized by Sansar Chand of Kangra.
Rewalsar Lake (Tso Pema) in Mandi is sacred to how many religions?     (a) One  (b) Two  (c) Three  (d) Four     Answer: (c) Three – Hinduism, Buddhism, and Sikhism all venerate this lake.

The first Param Vir Chakra of India was awarded (posthumously) to which soldier from HP?     (a) Lt. Ram Raghoba Rane  (b) Major Somnath Sharma  (c) Captain Vikram Batra  (d) Naik Jadunath Singh     Answer: (b) Major Somnath Sharma – from Dadh village, Kangra; died in action November 3, 1947.

Pin Valley National Park in Spiti is a habitat for:     (a) Tigers  (b) Asian Elephants  (c) Snow Leopards and Siberian Ibex  (d) Rhinoceros     Answer: (c) Snow Leopards and Siberian Ibex – cold desert national park.

Bir Billing in Kangra is world-famous for which adventure sport?     (a) River rafting  (b) Rock climbing  (c) Paragliding  (d) Skiing     Answer: (c) Paragliding – hosted the Paragliding World Cup; 'Paragliding Capital of India'.

The Nati dance of HP entered the Guinness Book of World Records for:     (a) Fastest dance  (b) Largest number of people performing traditional dance simultaneously  (c) Oldest dance form  (d) Most colourful dance     Answer: (b) Largest number of people performing traditional dance simultaneously.

The Manimahesh Yatra pilgrimage is associated with which deity?     (a) Lord Vishnu  (b) Goddess Durga  (c) Lord Shiva (Manimahesh Kailash)  (d) Guru Padmasambhava     Answer: (c) Lord Shiva – Manimahesh Kailash (5656 m) in Chamba; annual pilgrimage in Bhadon month.

Which HP district shares an international boundary with China (Tibet)?     (a) Lahaul-Spiti only  (b) Chamba only  (c) Kinnaur and Lahaul-Spiti  (d) Kinnaur, Lahaul-Spiti, and Chamba     Answer: (d) Kinnaur, Lahaul-Spiti, and Chamba – all share the border with Tibet.

The Nathpa Jhakri Hydroelectric Project with 1500 MW capacity is on which river?     (a) Beas  (b) Ravi  (c) Sutlej  (d) Chenab     Answer: (c) Sutlej – in Kinnaur/Shimla; largest hydropower project in HP.

Baddi-Barotiwala-Nalagarh (BBN) is the major industrial hub of HP and is located in which district?     (a) Shimla  (b) Hamirpur  (c) Solan  (d) Una     Answer: (c) Solan – known especially for pharmaceutical industries.
